reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes a PancakeSwap front-running bot while claiming immediate tenfold returns and profits of up to 100 BNB per day. It instructs viewers to deploy a contract, send 0.5 BNB, and press an Action control, while claiming that 90 percent will return to the wallet. The acknowledgment that fees can sometimes exceed profits does not change that the transfer is directly linked to the promised returns.

automatically locates any liquidity added to a BSC token, immediately buy and sell at profit
Today I'm going to be going over deploying a front-running bot on PancakeSwap with a wrapped BnB pair.
we're just gonna send some funds to that contract that we just created
For the sake of this video I'm just gonna do 0.5 bnb Actually might just make it 1.

opening.argument: The presentation includes a concrete risk warning rather than describing returns as risk-free. Its description explains that high burn fees can cause the contract to lose more in fees than it makes, and recommends funding levels intended to avoid that outcome. That qualification materially undercuts the idea that the speaker is promising a guaranteed result. The speaker also describes a specific automated process and fee exposure, including that 90 percent is returned while 10 percent remains in the pool, giving viewers information about how the claimed outcome is supposed to work rather than concealing all downside.

I recommend funding the contract with around 1 - 0.5 BNB just to make sure that won't happen.
10% of profit automatically reenters the front-run pool
automatically transacts back to your wallet 90% of the profit

rebuttal.rebuttal: The title and profit language are attention-grabbing, but they do not erase the explicit warning that fees can exceed profits. The description does not present every outcome as certain; it identifies token burn fees, gas fees, and inadequate funding as conditions that can produce a loss. The prosecution's selected funding quotes establish that a transfer occurs, but not that the transfer is deceptive or that loss is concealed.

citations.quote: If you fund the contract with 0.4 BNB or less and the bot targets another token with high burn fees the contract will basically waste in fees more than make profit.
Current parameters of this contract is that 10% of profit automatically reenters the front-run pool
For the sake of this video I'm just gonna do 0.5 bnb Actually might just make it 1.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A warning about fees does not neutralize the central claim that the funded contract produces rapid profit. The same description tells viewers to fund it with approximately 0.5 to 1 BNB, while the title promises making ten times instantly. The warning narrows one possible failure condition, but it leaves the advertised profit mechanism and the requested transfer intact.

immediately buy and sell at profit

opening.argument: The material is structured as an operational technology demonstration: the speaker explains how to compile Solidity, connect Remix to a wallet, deploy a contract, and inspect the resulting address on BSC Scan. The narration repeatedly describes what is being done in the interface, including compiling, deploying, funding, and activating the contract. That is consistent with a tutorial or demonstration of a blockchain tool. The supplied frames likewise show Remix's compiler and deployment panels and BSC Scan pages, supporting a software-workflow reading rather than independently proving that the advertised financial outcome is genuine.

We're gonna do injected web 3
we're going to deploy this to our wallet
Next thing that we do after its sent to the contract we we'll just go over here, and press the Action button

rebuttal.rebuttal: The operational walkthrough is more than incidental background: the speaker explains the contract's code context, deployment interface, wallet connection, and activation sequence. The prosecution interprets those steps as solicitation, but the same steps can be understood as demonstrating how a smart-contract workflow operates. Claims about possible performance remain claims made during a demonstration, and the supplied material does not independently verify that the stated returns occurred.

so. We're gonna do injected web 3. Make sure that your wallet is connected to remix
We're gonna do injected web 3

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Calling the walkthrough a tutorial does not change what viewers are instructed to do. The speaker tells them to fund the newly created contract, press Action, and expects a deposit back, while describing the bot as automatically buying and selling for profit. Those are operational instructions tied directly to the promised financial result, not merely neutral code education.

it engages all the constructors that are built as far as engaging the pancake router, it automatically buys and sells for you.
We usually only need to wait a couple minutes before we get back a deposit

opening.argument: This can be framed as promotion of a software-and-deployment workflow with ordinary access links and operational prerequisites, not proof that a seller is collecting money through a hidden payout scheme. The description directs viewers to public tools including Remix, MetaMask, and Binance Smart Chain connection instructions. It explains a contract-based trading process and identifies gas and burn fees as costs. The supplied material does not show a request for a password, seed phrase, or recruitment of additional participants; it describes sending funds to a contract and interacting with a visible Action function. That distinction matters when deciding whether the content establishes a deceptive mechanism rather than a risky tool demonstration.

citations.quote: Access Remix: https://remixcompiler.com/
Get MetaMask: https://metamask.io/download.html
Connect MetaMask to Binance Smart Chain
It will automatically sell within one minute and then from there it will take 90

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution treats any funding as proof of a scam mechanism, but funding a deployed contract is also the stated operational input for the described tool. The sources identify a visible contract, a wallet connection, gas fees, burn fees, and an Action function; they do not show that the creator obtains the wallet's credentials or secretly controls the viewer's wallet. A risky or aggressive trading workflow is not by itself proof of deceptive collection.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The absence of a password request does not make the funding mechanism ordinary or safe. The content asks viewers to send 0.5 or 1 BNB to a newly created contract, activate it, and expect a deposit back, while claiming immediate tenfold results and as much as 100 BNB per day. A visible transaction can still be the mechanism by which funds are solicited for an unsupported return.
